newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India sells May Cochin naphtha to Vitol at -$40/T.
newsitem.headline: India sells May Cochin naphtha to Vitol at -$40/T.

text.p: State-owned Indian Oil Corp (IOC) sold by tender 30,000 tonnes of high aromatic naphtha (HAN) at a record low price of around $40 a tonne below Japanese spot quotes, for May 6-7 lifting free-on-board (fob) Cochin on the west coast, industry sources said on Monday.
The cargo was sold to Dutch trader Vitol, they said.
"It is a very low price," one trader said.
The tender closed on April 24 and bids were valid for one day.

IOC's last HAN cargo for April 1-3 lifting from Cochin was sold at a discount of $19.08 to Japanese spot quotes, fob. This was within range of the $16-$20 discount that IOC received for its Cochin HAN cargoes last year, traders said.
They said the low price received in the latest tender was due to poor demand for HAN, which is used in the production of gasoline.
Gasoline has also been suffering from low prices.

An industry source said this was IOC's second attempt to get a good price for the cargo which was initially offered for April 30-May 2 lifting in a tender which was then cancelled due to low bid prices.
IOC then re-offered the product in a fresh tender, but increased the volume to 30,000 tonnes and moved the lifting dates to May 6-7 in an attempt to get better prices.
